title: Fronting 主題／賓語前置句
titleEn: Using fronting to foreground a topic or object

source.file: Sentence Structure 168 -「Fronting 句：主題／賓語前置句」.pdf
omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.

formula: Topic / Object + comma + Subject + Verb + other information

formulas.formula: Topic / Object + comma + Subject + Verb + other information
Topic + comma + complete clause containing a pronoun referring to the topic

examples.en: This person, I don’t know him at all.
examples.zh: 這個人，我完全不認識他。
examples.highlight: This person, I don’t know him at all.

rules.zh: 標準 Fronting 不重複賓語 不是： 在 Pattern A 中，賓語已經移到句首，原本的位置不應再加入 it、him、her 或 them。
rules.en: Standard fronting does not repeat the object. In Pattern A, once the object has moved to the beginning, do not add it, him, her or them again in its original position.

rules.zh: 口語 Pattern B 可以使用代名詞 在標示為 [Spoken 口語] 的題目中，可以用代名詞再次指向句首主題： 這種說法在談話中自然，但一般不適合在正式作文、報告或學術文章中頻繁使用。
rules.en: Spoken Pattern B may use a pronoun to refer back to the fronted topic. This sounds natural in conversation, but it is generally unsuitable for frequent use in formal essays, reports or academic writing.

rules.zh: 前置部分後面通常使用逗號 逗號把句首主題和主要句子分開，讓結構更容易理解。
rules.en: Normally use a comma after the fronted element. The comma separates the opening topic from the main sentence and makes the structure easier to understand.

rules.zh: 整個重要詞組應一起移動 不要只移動其中一個字：
rules.en: Move the whole important phrase together, not only one word. For example, front The final chapter as a unit in The final chapter, I enjoyed.

rules.zh: 時態、否定和情態動詞必須保留 cannot、have、had、will、may、should 等重要意思不能因改寫而消失。
rules.en: Preserve tense, negation and modal verbs. Important meanings carried by cannot, have, had, will, may, should and similar words must not disappear during the rewrite.
examples: They cannot change this decision now.

rules.zh: Fronting 不等於倒裝句 Fronting 後面的主語和動詞通常仍維持正常次序： 不是：
rules.en: Fronting is not the same as inversion. After the fronted element, the subject and verb normally retain their usual order.

rules.zh: Fronting 應有明確目的 Fronting 通常用來： 突出某個重點； 回應剛才提到的主題； 比較兩項事物； 表達接受一方面、拒絕另一方面； 製造較鮮明的口語語氣。 它不需要在每一句中使用。過度使用會令文章顯得刻意或戲劇化。
rules.en: Use fronting for a clear purpose: to highlight a key point, respond to a topic just mentioned, compare two things, accept one aspect while rejecting another, or create a more vivid conversational tone. It is not needed in every sentence; overuse can make writing sound forced or dramatic.

benefits.zh: 讓重要主題立即成為焦點 讀者首先看到句首內容，因此會自然地把注意力放在該人物、事物或問題上。 兩句的基本意思相同，但第二句特別強調 that part。
benefits.en: It puts the important topic in the spotlight. Because readers see the fronted content first, their attention naturally goes to that person, thing or issue. I completely understand that part and That part, I completely understand have the same basic meaning, but the second especially emphasises that part.

benefits.zh: 讓對比更加清楚 Fronting 可以把兩個對比項目放在相同位置： 讀者可以立即看出「第一個例子」和「第二個例子」得到不同處理。
benefits.en: It makes contrasts easier to see by placing contrasting items in the same fronted position: The first example, I can explain, but the second one, I cannot. The reader immediately sees that the two examples receive different treatment.
examples: The first example, I can explain, but the second one, I cannot.

benefits.zh: 幫助你直接回應某個主題 當別人剛剛提到一件事時，你可以把該主題放在句首： 這種說法能清楚表示：「現在我要評論的是新時間表。」
benefits.en: It helps you respond directly to a topic just mentioned. The new timetable, I fully support clearly signals, “The new timetable is what I am commenting on now.”
examples: The new timetable, I fully support.

benefits.zh: 增加句子開頭的變化 學生經常以 I、we、they 或 the company 開始每一句。Fronting 能改變句子的排列方式，使連續句 子不會全部使用相同開頭。
benefits.en: It gives you another sentence opening. Learners often begin every sentence with I, we, they or the company; fronting changes the arrangement so consecutive sentences do not all begin in the same way.

benefits.zh: 提供容易運用的說話框架 你可以利用以下框架快速組織回應： 這個框架特別適合用來表達有保留的同意、比較或反駁。
benefits.en: It provides a useful speaking frame, such as This part, I understand, but that part, I don't or The price, I can accept, but the waiting time, I cannot. The frame is especially useful for qualified agreement, comparison or rebuttal.
examples: The price, I can accept, but the waiting time, I cannot.
